title: Run a 7-Day Instagram Growth Experiment
description: Run a structured 7-day experiment on your Instagram account — plan content, create and post daily, track metrics, and analyze what works. This is your first real social media campaign with data-driven decisions.
prerequisites: Instagram account (personal or brand — at least 1 week old)
CapCut or InShot for Reels editing (phone app)
Completed Module 2 notes on Instagram algorithm and content formats
learning_outcomes: Audit an Instagram profile and set baseline metrics
Plan a week of mixed-format content (Reels, Stories, Posts)
Create platform-native content using Canva and CapCut
Track daily metrics and understand Instagram analytics
Analyze results and form data-backed hypotheses for improvement

steps.title: Audit Current Profile and Set Baseline Metrics
steps.instructions:
1. Open your Instagram account on desktop (for easier data access) or use the mobile app's Professional Dashboard.

2. Switch to a Professional Account if you have not already:
   - Go to Settings > Account > Switch to Professional Account
   - Choose 'Creator' (for personal brand) or 'Business' (for a brand page)
   - This unlocks Instagram Insights — essential for tracking

3. Record your BASELINE METRICS (before the experiment starts):
   Create a Google Sheet called 'Instagram Growth Experiment — [YourHandle]'
   Tab 1: 'Baseline' with these fields:

   | Metric | Current Number | Date Recorded |
   |--------|---------------|---------------|
   | Total Followers | ___ | ___ |
   | Total Posts | ___ | ___ |
   | Average Likes (last 10 posts) | ___ | ___ |
   | Average Comments (last 10 posts) | ___ | ___ |
   | Engagement Rate | ___ | ___ |
   | Average Reel Views (last 5 Reels) | ___ | ___ |
   | Profile Visits (last 7 days) | ___ | ___ |
   | Accounts Reached (last 7 days) | ___ | ___ |
   | Website Clicks (last 7 days) | ___ | ___ |

   To calculate Engagement Rate:
   (Average Likes + Average Comments) / Total Followers x 100
   Example: (45 + 5) / 1000 x 100 = 5% engagement rate

4. PROFILE AUDIT — Check these elements:
   - [ ] Profile photo: Clear, professional, matches other platforms?
   - [ ] Username: Easy to spell, search-friendly?
   - [ ] Bio: Clearly says who you are, what you do, includes CTA?
   - [ ] Bio link: Active and relevant (use Linktree if you have multiple links)?
   - [ ] Highlights: Organized, cover images match brand?
   - [ ] Feed aesthetic: Is there a consistent color/style?
   - [ ] Last post date: How recent?

5. Fix any profile issues BEFORE starting the experiment. Your profile is your landing page — if it is not optimized, even great content will not convert visitors to followers.

6. Set your EXPERIMENT GOALS (realistic for 7 days):
   - Follower goal: Current + ___% growth (aim for 5-15% for small accounts)
   - Engagement goal: Increase engagement rate by ___% 
   - Reach goal: Reach ___ new accounts
   - Content goal: Post ___ pieces of content in 7 days

Write these goals in your spreadsheet. You will compare against them on Day 8.

Self-check: Can you clearly see your Instagram Insights? If not, your account may be too new (needs 7 days as Professional) or you may need to switch account type. Ask a classmate to help troubleshoot if needed.

steps.title: Plan 7 Days of Content (Mix of Reels, Stories, Posts)
steps.instructions:
1. Create Tab 2 in your spreadsheet: 'Content Plan' with these columns:
   | Day | Date | Content Type | Topic | Format | Hook | CTA | Hashtags | Post Time | Status |

2. Plan your 7 days of content using this structure:

   DAY 1 (Monday) — REEL (Educational)
   - Topic: Teach one quick tip related to your niche
   - Length: 30-45 seconds
   - Hook: Start with a bold statement or question
   - CTA: 'Follow for daily [niche] tips'
   - Post time: 8:30 AM or 7:30 PM IST

   DAY 2 (Tuesday) — CAROUSEL (Value)
   - Topic: 5 tips/myths/steps related to your niche
   - Slides: 8-10
   - Hook (Slide 1): Number + benefit ('5 [things] that will [benefit]')
   - CTA: 'Save this and share with a friend who needs it'
   - Post time: 12:00 PM IST

   DAY 3 (Wednesday) — STORIES SERIES (Engagement)
   - 5-7 Stories across the day:
     Story 1: Share something from your day (behind the scenes)
     Story 2: Ask a question or poll related to your niche
     Story 3: Share a tip (text on colorful background)
     Story 4: Share a resource or tool recommendation
     Story 5: 'DM me [word] for [something free]' or quiz sticker
   - Goal: Get replies and poll votes

   DAY 4 (Thursday) — REEL (Trending/Relatable)
   - Topic: Use a trending audio with educational overlay
   - Length: 15-30 seconds
   - Hook: Visual hook in first 1 second (movement, text, surprise)
   - CTA: 'Relatable? Double tap!'
   - Post time: 9:00 AM IST

   DAY 5 (Friday) — SINGLE IMAGE POST (Personal)
   - Topic: Share a personal story, lesson, or behind-the-scenes
   - Caption: 200-300 words, storytelling format (Hook-Story-Lesson-CTA)
   - Image: Selfie, workspace, or phone screenshot
   - CTA: 'What is your experience? Comment below'
   - Post time: 6:00 PM IST

   DAY 6 (Saturday) — REEL (How-To/Tutorial)
   - Topic: Show how to do something (screen recording or talking head)
   - Length: 45-60 seconds
   - Hook: 'Here is how to [achieve result] in [time]'
   - CTA: 'Save this for when you need it'
   - Post time: 10:00 AM IST

   DAY 7 (Sunday) — CAROUSEL + STORIES (Wrap-up)
   - Carousel: Summarize your week's learnings or recap your best tips
   - Stories: Share your growth experiment results (builds transparency and trust)
   - CTA: 'Follow along for next week's content'
   - Post time: 11:00 AM IST

3. For each day, also plan:
   - 10 relevant hashtags (mix of: 3 broad, 4 niche-specific, 3 location-based)
   - 5 accounts to engage with BEFORE posting (comment on their posts, reply to their stories)
   - 1 reply strategy: How will you respond to comments within 30 minutes?

4. Save your content plan. This is your roadmap for the next 7 days.

Self-check: Does your plan include at least 3 Reels (Instagram's most-pushed format), at least 1 carousel (high save rate), and daily Stories (keeps you visible)? If not, adjust.

steps.title: Create and Schedule All Content
steps.instructions:
1. BATCH CREATE all content in one sitting (this is how professionals work — saves time and maintains consistency).

2. CREATE YOUR REELS (Days 1, 4, 6):

   For each Reel:
   a) Write the full script (use the format from Lab 02-A, Step 4)
   b) Record the video:
      - Use your phone camera (back camera = better quality, front = easier framing)
      - Find good lighting (face a window during daytime)
      - Record in a quiet environment
      - Record 2-3 takes of each — pick the best
      - Record vertically (9:16 ratio)
   c) Edit in CapCut:
      - Import your clips
      - Trim start and end (remove hesitation)
      - Add text overlays (your key points)
      - Add captions (CapCut auto-captions > edit for accuracy)
      - Add trending or suitable background music (lower volume so voice is clear)
      - Export in highest quality
   d) Write the caption and hashtags in your spreadsheet

3. CREATE YOUR CAROUSELS (Days 2, 7):

   For each Carousel:
   a) Open Canva > Create > Custom size: 1080x1350 (or 1080x1080)
   b) Design Slide 1 (HOOK): This determines if people swipe. Use:
      - Bold, large text (main benefit or curiosity)
      - Contrasting colors
      - Your face or an eye-catching image
   c) Design content slides (one idea per slide, maximum 30 words)
   d) Design last slide (CTA + your handle)
   e) Check consistency: Same fonts, colors, and spacing throughout
   f) Export as PNG (individual slides for upload)
   g) Write the caption: Hook line + valuable body + CTA + hashtags

4. CREATE YOUR IMAGE POST (Day 5):
   - Take or select a personal/authentic photo
   - Write the 200-300 word caption in your notes app
   - Draft, edit, and finalize

5. PLAN YOUR STORIES (Days 3, 7):
   - Create 2-3 Story graphics in Canva (1080x1920 px)
   - Plan which stickers to use (poll, quiz, question box, slider)
   - Write text for each Story frame

6. ORGANIZE EVERYTHING:
   - Create a folder on your phone: 'Instagram Experiment'
   - Sub-folders: Day1, Day2, Day3... Day7
   - Put each day's content (video, images, captions) in the right folder
   - This way you just open the folder each morning and post

7. OPTIONAL — SCHEDULE (if you use a scheduling tool):
   - Use Meta Business Suite (free) to schedule posts up to 75 days in advance
   - Or use Later/Buffer free plan
   - Note: Scheduling Reels sometimes reduces initial reach; posting manually may be better

Self-check: Open your phone's photo gallery. Can you see all 7 days of content ready to post? Is every caption written and saved? If you answered yes to both, you are ready to execute.

steps.title: Track Daily Metrics (Reach, Engagement, Followers)
steps.instructions:
1. Create Tab 3 in your spreadsheet: 'Daily Tracking' with these columns:

   | Day | Date | Followers (start) | Followers (end) | New Followers | Content Posted | Likes | Comments | Shares | Saves | Reach | Profile Visits | Notes |

2. DAILY TRACKING ROUTINE (do this every night at 10 PM IST):

   Step 1: Open Instagram > Professional Dashboard > Insights
   Step 2: Note down today's numbers in the spreadsheet
   Step 3: Check individual post performance:
   - For each post/Reel published today, note: likes, comments, shares, saves, reach
   Step 4: Note your follower count (did it go up or down?)
   Step 5: Write 1-2 observations in the 'Notes' column

3. WHAT TO TRACK FOR EACH CONTENT TYPE:

   Reels:
   - Views (most important for Reels)
   - Watch time / Average watch percentage
   - Likes, Comments, Shares, Saves
   - Reach (accounts reached vs followers)
   - How many new followers came from this Reel?

   Carousels:
   - Reach
   - Saves (most important for carousels — high saves = algorithm boost)
   - Shares
   - Comments
   - Swipe-through rate (how many people swiped to the last slide?)

   Stories:
   - Views / Reach
   - Replies / DMs received
   - Poll votes / Quiz answers
   - Tap-forward rate (high = boring) vs Tap-back rate (high = interesting)
   - Exits (which Story did people leave on?)

   Image Post:
   - Likes, Comments
   - Saves and Shares
   - Reach

4. ENGAGEMENT TRACKING (do this alongside posting):
   - Track: How many accounts did YOU engage with today? (comments on others' posts)
   - Track: How quickly did you reply to comments on your posts?
   - Track: How many DMs did you receive/send?
   - These 'input' activities directly affect your 'output' results

5. Also note any external factors:
   - Was there a festival or trending topic that affected engagement?
   - Did you post at a different time than planned? Why?
   - Did any Reel get pushed by the algorithm unexpectedly?
   - Did you change anything from your original plan?

6. Take SCREENSHOTS of your insights dashboard each day (save in your experiment folder). These serve as proof and make your final report more visual.

Self-check: After 3 days, look at your data. Can you already see a pattern? (e.g., Reels getting more reach than carousels, morning posts doing better than evening). Write down your initial hypothesis — you will test it in the remaining days.

steps.title: Analyze Results and Write a Report
steps.instructions:
1. On Day 8 (the day after your experiment ends), sit down with your complete data and write an analysis report.

2. Create Tab 4 in your spreadsheet: 'Results Summary'

   OVERALL PERFORMANCE:
   | Metric | Before (Baseline) | After (Day 8) | Change | % Change |
   |--------|-------------------|---------------|--------|----------|
   | Followers | ___ | ___ | +/- ___ | ___% |
   | Avg Engagement Rate | ___% | ___% | +/- ___% | |
   | Total Reach (7 days) | ___ | ___ accounts | | |
   | Total Likes (7 days) | ___ | | | |
   | Total Comments (7 days) | ___ | | | |
   | Total Saves (7 days) | ___ | | | |
   | Profile Visits (7 days) | ___ | | | |

3. CONTENT PERFORMANCE RANKING:
   Rank all 7 days of content from best to worst performing:
   | Rank | Day | Content Type | Reach | Engagement | Key Insight |

4. ANSWER THESE ANALYSIS QUESTIONS (write 2-3 sentences for each):

   a) Which content FORMAT performed best? (Reel vs Carousel vs Post vs Stories)
      - Evidence: [cite specific numbers]

   b) Which content TOPIC got the most engagement?
      - Evidence: [cite specific numbers]

   c) What posting TIME worked best?
      - Evidence: [compare morning vs afternoon vs evening posts]

   d) Did hashtags make a difference? Which hashtags brought discovery?
      - Evidence: [check 'From Hashtags' in reach breakdown]

   e) How did your engagement with others affect your own reach?
      - Evidence: [compare days you engaged a lot vs days you did not]

   f) What surprised you? (something you did not expect)

   g) What would you do differently next week?

5. WRITE YOUR REPORT (500-700 words) with these sections:

   Section 1: Experiment Setup
   - What was your goal?
   - What content did you plan?
   - What was your strategy?

   Section 2: Results
   - Key numbers (use the table above)
   - Best and worst performing content
   - Goal achieved or not? By how much?

   Section 3: Key Learnings
   - Top 3 things you learned about Instagram
   - Top 3 things you learned about YOUR audience specifically
   - What the data tells you about what to do next

   Section 4: Next Steps
   - What will you continue doing? (what worked)
   - What will you stop doing? (what did not work)
   - What will you try next? (new experiments)

6. COMPILE YOUR FINAL SUBMISSION:
   - Google Sheet with all 4 tabs (Baseline, Content Plan, Daily Tracking, Results)
   - Screenshots folder (daily insights screenshots)
   - Written report (Google Doc, 500-700 words)
   - Links to your posted content (or screenshots of each post)

7. SHARE YOUR LEARNINGS:
   - Turn your experiment results into a LinkedIn post or Instagram carousel
   - This is meta-content: sharing what you learned about content creation IS content
   - This transparency builds trust and positions you as someone who practices what they preach

Self-check: Does your report include specific NUMBERS (not just feelings)? Could someone reading your report replicate your experiment? If yes to both, you have completed a professional-grade growth experiment.

Congratulations — you have just done what social media managers at agencies do every month for their clients. The only difference is they get paid for it. You are building that skill right now.
